commits_data.title: dfilter: Improve grammar to parse functions
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Improve grammar to parse functions

A function is an identifier that is followed by '(' and ')' according
to some grammatical rules. Don't assume a token is a function just
because it matches a display filter function name.

Before:

  % dftest 'foobar(http.user_agent) contains "UPDATE"'
  Filter: "foobar(http.user_agent) contains "UPDATE""
  dftest: Syntax error.

After:

  % dftest 'foobar(http.user_agent) contains "UPDATE"'
  Filter: "foobar(http.user_agent) contains "UPDATE""
  dftest: The function 'foobar' does not exist.

commits_data.title: dfilter: Save token value to syntax tree
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Save token value to syntax tree

When parsing we save the token value to the syntax tree. This is
useful for better error reporting. Use it to report an invalid
entity for the slice operation. Before only the memory location
was reported, which is not a good error message.

Before:
  % dftest '"01:02:03:04"[0:3] == foo'
  Filter: ""01:02:03:04"[0:3] == foo"
  dftest: Range is not supported for entity <0x7f6c84017740> of type STRING

After:
  % dftest '"01:02:03:04"[0:3] == foo'
  Filter: ""01:02:03:04"[0:3] == foo"
  dftest: Range is not supported for entity 01:02:03:04 of type STRING

When creating a new node from an old one we need to copy the token
value. Simple tokens such as RBRACKET, COMMA and COLON are
not part of the AST and don't have an associated semantic value.

commits_data.title: dfilter: Add unit test for "exists" and fix it
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Add unit test for "exists" and fix it

The expression "frame" is failing with "frame is not a valid
protocol" and this is not caught in the dfilter tests.

  % dftest "frame"
  Filter: "frame"
  dftest: "frame" is neither a field nor a protocol name.

Add a new display filter test for "exists" (test the existance
of a protocol field).

Fix the code by making sure an "exists" filter tries to parse
an unparsed string as a protocol field.

  % dftest "frame"
  Filter: "frame"

  Constants:

  Instructions:
  00000 CHECK_EXISTS	frame
  00001 RETURN

  % dftest "foobar"
  Filter: "foobar"
  dftest: "foobar" is neither a field nor a protocol name.

Add checkDfilterSucceed() to the test suite to test a successful
parse using dftest.

Put the new test in a new test group because this simple test didn't
seem to fit in any of the other groups. It might need a better name
than 'group_field' in the future.

commits_data.title: dfilter: Parse protocol fields at the semantic level
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Parse protocol fields at the semantic level

Instead of parsing any blob of characters that matches a registered
protocol field as such in the lexer do it at the semantic level
because the meaning of "unparsed data" is contextual and sometimes
the meaning of unparsed does not include "protocol field", such as
on the right side of a matches relation.

For example the expression "udp.payload matches tcp" fails with
"protocol is invalid on the right-side of comparison", where the
intention of allowing unparsed strings (strings not encased in
double quotes) is to interpret the blob of bytes { 't', 'c', 'p'}
as a string in a context where protocol fields don't make sense
(for the sake of flexibility presumably).

A fix was added in ac0b1d42f314b752d87c9d583d6bd66e8140f534 for
check_relation() but instead of trying to catch the parse mistake
in one or more places remove the field concept from the grammar
and use the appropriate heuristic at the semantic level.

Ping #12810.
